intro: Hi! In English some words simply go together: we make a mistake, do our homework, tell the truth and take a photo. In this lesson you'll learn the most useful partners of make and do, say, tell, speak and talk, and have, take and get, so you stop translating word by word. Warm-up: how do you say 'minum obat' in English?
teachingNotes: Explain 'collocation' plainly the first time: kolokasi = kata yang biasa dipasangkan (word partners). There often isn't a logic (make a mistake, not *do a mistake): learners should learn verb + noun as one chunk and write new nouns down with their verb (not 'decision' but 'make a decision'). The core Indonesian trap is word-by-word translation: membuat/melakukan don't map onto make/do (melakukan kesalahan → *do a mistake), bilang can be say or tell, minum obat is take medicine (not *drink medicine), ambil foto is take a photo (the node's common error *'Let's make a photo').

make vs do: give the ROUGH guide and say it has exceptions. make ≈ create/produce something new: make a mistake, a decision, a plan, a phone call, money, noise, coffee, a cake, breakfast/dinner. do ≈ tasks, jobs, activities, often routine or duty: do homework (already met in a2-vocab-work-study: recap, don't reteach), the dishes, the shopping, the laundry, exercise, a course, business, your best; also do + something/nothing/anything (What are you doing?). Exceptions to name: make the bed (housework but make), make breakfast vs do the cooking, make a phone call / make a mistake (no 'creating', just chunks). Common error: *'I have to make my homework' → do my homework. Variants that are also correct, so never test them against each other: take a decision (British) = make a decision; take a course = do a course; take/get exercise (UK/US) = do exercise; give/do/make a presentation.

say / tell / speak / talk: tell + the PERSON who hears (tell me, tell your boss) and the fixed chunks tell a story / a joke / the truth / a lie. say + the WORDS (say hello, say sorry, say goodbye, say something, say that again); to add the person use to: say sorry to Rina. Common error: *'Can you say me the answer?' → tell me the answer. speak + a language (speak English, not *talk English) and in formal situations (Can I speak to the manager, please?). talk = a conversation: talk to/with someone, talk about something. speak to / talk to and speak about / talk about are both correct (speak sounds more formal or serious): never build a question where both are options.

have / take / get + noun: have + meals, events and experiences (have breakfast, a meeting, a party, a good time, a rest; here have is not 'punya'). take + photos, transport, medicine, breaks, seats (take a photo, a taxi, the KRL, an ojek, medicine, a break, a seat; 'an ojek' because ojek starts with a vowel sound). get = receive / obtain / become / arrive (get a message, a job, better, tired, home; no 'to' before home: get home but get to the office). Pairs where BOTH are fine, so accept either and never test one against the other: have/take a shower, have/take a break, have/take a look, have/take a seat, get/take a taxi or the bus, have a rest / get some rest / take a rest, take a job (accept an offer) vs get a job. British English uses have a bit more, American English take.

Grammar limits: use A0–A2 grammar (present and past simple and continuous, present perfect, will, going to, can/could, should, have to). Do NOT teach reported speech with say/tell (*She told me that she was tired*, *He told me to wait*): that's b1-reported-speech-intro; direct quotes like Rina said, 'Good morning!' are fine. No passive, no second conditional, no relative clauses beyond fixed phrases. Don't add more collocation families (strong coffee, heavy rain, catch a cold) unless the learner asks; keep to these nine verbs.

keyPoints.title: make or do
keyPoints.explanation: Word partners (collocations) are words that usually go together, often without logic, so learn them as chunks. Rough guide: make = create or produce something (make a mistake, a decision, a plan, a phone call, money, noise, coffee); do = tasks, jobs and activities (do homework, the dishes, the shopping, exercise, a course, business, your best). Exceptions exist: make the bed. Not 'make my homework', not 'do a mistake'.

examples.en: I made a mistake in the sales report.
examples.id: Saya membuat kesalahan di laporan penjualan.

examples.en: Can you do the shopping after work?
We need to make a plan for the launch.
examples.id: Kita perlu membuat rencana untuk peluncurannya.

id.title: make atau do
id.explanation: Pasangan kata (kolokasi) adalah kata-kata yang biasa dipakai bersama, sering tanpa logika, jadi hafalkan sebagai satu paket. Panduan kasar: make = menciptakan atau menghasilkan sesuatu (make a mistake, a decision, a plan, a phone call, money, noise, coffee); do = tugas, pekerjaan dan kegiatan (do homework, the dishes, the shopping, exercise, a course, business, your best). Ada pengecualian: make the bed (merapikan tempat tidur). Bukan 'make my homework', bukan 'do a mistake'.

keyPoints.title: say, tell, speak or talk
keyPoints.explanation: tell + the person who hears (tell me, tell your boss), and tell a story / a joke / the truth / a lie. say + the words (say hello, say sorry, say something); to add the person use to: say sorry to Rina. Never 'say me'. speak + a language (speak English) or in formal situations (Can I speak to the manager?). talk = a conversation: talk to someone, talk about something.

examples.en: Can you tell me the answer?
My manager speaks English and Mandarin.
examples.id: Manajer saya bisa berbahasa Inggris dan Mandarin.

id.title: say, tell, speak atau talk
id.explanation: tell + orang yang mendengar (tell me, tell your boss), dan tell a story / a joke / the truth / a lie (bercerita, melucu, berkata jujur, berbohong). say + kata-katanya (say hello, say sorry, say something); untuk menyebut orangnya pakai to: say sorry to Rina. Jangan pernah 'say me'. speak + bahasa (speak English) atau di situasi resmi (Can I speak to the manager?). talk = percakapan, ngobrol: talk to someone, talk about something.

keyPoints.title: have, take and get + noun
keyPoints.explanation: have + meals, events and experiences: have breakfast, have a meeting, have a party, have a good time, have a rest (here have doesn't mean 'punya'). take + photos, transport, medicine and breaks: take a photo, take a taxi, take medicine, take a break. get = receive, find, become or arrive: get a message, get a job, get better, get home. Some pairs both work: have/take a shower.

examples.en: Let's take a photo in front of the hotel.
We have a team meeting every Monday.
Rina got a job at a bank in Surabaya.
examples.id: Rina dapat kerja di sebuah bank di Surabaya.

id.title: have, take dan get + kata benda
id.explanation: have + makan, acara dan pengalaman: have breakfast (sarapan), have a meeting (rapat), have a party, have a good time (bersenang-senang), have a rest (istirahat). Di sini have bukan 'punya'. take + foto, kendaraan, obat dan jeda: take a photo, take a taxi, take medicine (minum obat), take a break. get = menerima, mendapat, menjadi atau sampai: get a message, get a job, get better (membaik), get home (sampai rumah). Ada pasangan yang dua-duanya benar: have/take a shower (mandi).

assessment.prompt: Complete with make or do: Pak Hasan has to ___ a decision about the new office before Friday.
assessment.rubric: Correct: make (make a decision = mengambil keputusan; you create a choice in your head). 'do' = 0. 'makes' or 'made' = 50 (right verb, wrong form after has to). 'take' = 60 (British 'take a decision' exists, but the item asks for make or do).

assessment.prompt: Complete with the correct form of make or do: In our house, my brother always ___ the dishes after dinner.
assessment.rubric: Correct: does (do the dishes = mencuci piring, a housework task; my brother = he, so -es). 'do' = 50 (right verb, missing -es). 'did' = 50. 'makes' or 'make' = 0.

could you tell me the way to the station
can you tell me the way to the station please
could you tell me the way to the station please

assessment.rubric: Correct: Can you tell me the way to the station? (a person right after the verb → tell). 'Can you say the way to the station?' = 20 (removes the person but say still isn't natural here). 'Can you say to me the way …' = 30. 'Can you show me the way to the station?' = 70 (natural English, but tell was the point). Unchanged = 0.

assessment.rubric: Correct: speaks (speak + a language; she → -s). 'can speak' is also fine. 'speak' = 50 (missing -s). 'talks' = 0 (we don't say talk Japanese). 'says' or 'tells' = 0.

could you take a photo of us in front of monas

could you take a picture of us in front of monas
excuse me can you take a photo of us in front of monas

assessment.rubric: Correct: … could you take a photo of us in front of Monas? (take a photo = memotret, not make). 'take a picture' is fine. 'do a photo' or 'have a photo' = 0. 'take photo' (no a) = 70. Unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the correct form of have, take or get: The traffic was terrible, so Budi didn't ___ home until 9 p.m.
assessment.rubric: Correct: get (get home = sampai rumah, arrive; after didn't use the base form). 'got' = 50 (didn't + base form). 'get to home' = 60 (no to before home). 'have' or 'take' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the correct form of have, take or get: Sari is ___ a party at her kos on Saturday. Do you want to come?
assessment.rubric: Correct: having (have a party = mengadakan pesta; is + -ing for a future arrangement). 'have' or 'has' = 40 (right verb, wrong form after is). 'making' or 'doing' = 0. 'taking' or 'getting' = 0.

material.title: Word partners: why not 'do a mistake'?

blocks.text:
Some English words simply **go together**. We say **make a mistake**, not *do a mistake*; **take a photo**, not *make a photo*; **tell me**, not *say me*. These word partners are called **collocations**: words that people usually use together. Often there's **no logic**: it's just what English speakers say.

The trap for Indonesian speakers is translating word by word. *Membuat* and *melakukan* don't match make and do neatly (*melakukan kesalahan* is still **make** a mistake); *bilang* can be **say** or **tell**; and we *minum obat*, but in English you **take** medicine. So learn each verb + noun as **one chunk**, like one long word: *make-a-mistake*, *do-the-dishes*, *take-a-photo*.

id.text:
Ada kata-kata dalam bahasa Inggris yang memang **selalu berpasangan**. Orang bilang **make a mistake** (membuat kesalahan), bukan *do a mistake*; **take a photo** (memotret), bukan *make a photo*; **tell me** (kasih tahu aku), bukan *say me*. Pasangan kata seperti ini disebut **kolokasi** (collocation): kata-kata yang biasa dipakai bersama. Sering kali **tidak ada logikanya**: memang begitulah penutur bahasa Inggris bicara.

Jebakan buat kita adalah menerjemahkan kata per kata. *Membuat* dan *melakukan* tidak pas dengan make dan do (*melakukan kesalahan* tetap **make** a mistake); *bilang* bisa **say** atau **tell**; dan kita *minum obat*, tapi dalam bahasa Inggris obat itu di-**take**. Jadi hafalkan setiap kata kerja + kata benda sebagai **satu paket**, seperti satu kata panjang: *make-a-mistake*, *do-the-dishes*, *take-a-photo*.

rows.en: I made a mistake in the email.
rows.id: Saya membuat kesalahan di email itu.

rows.en: Have you done your homework?
rows.id: Kamu sudah mengerjakan PR-mu?

rows.en: Can you tell me your name again?
rows.id: Bisa sebutkan namamu lagi?

rows.en: Don't forget to take your medicine.
rows.id: Jangan lupa minum obatmu.

blocks.text: How to learn collocations: when you meet a new noun, write it down **with its verb**. Not just *decision* (keputusan), but **make a decision**; not just *break* (jeda), but **take a break**. When you read or listen, notice which verb comes before the noun. Little by little, the right partner starts to 'sound right'.

id.text: Cara belajar kolokasi: kalau ketemu kata benda baru, catat **bersama kata kerjanya**. Jangan cuma *decision* (keputusan), tapi **make a decision**; jangan cuma *break* (jeda), tapi **take a break**. Saat membaca atau mendengar, perhatikan kata kerja apa yang muncul sebelum kata bendanya. Lama-lama pasangan yang benar akan 'terdengar pas'.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence sounds natural in English?
options: I did a big mistake in my report.
I made a big mistake in my report.
blocks.explain: The partner of mistake is make: make a mistake. Indonesian melakukan kesalahan tempts people to say do, but English doesn't use do with mistake.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang terdengar alami dalam bahasa Inggris?
id.explain: Pasangan kata mistake adalah make: make a mistake. Bahasa Indonesia melakukan kesalahan membuat orang tergoda pakai do, tapi bahasa Inggris tidak memakai do dengan mistake.

id.title: Pasangan kata: kenapa bukan 'do a mistake'?

material.title: make or do? A rough guide

blocks.text:
Here's a rough guide (*panduan kasar*: it works most of the time, not always):
- **make** ≈ you **create or produce** something that wasn't there before: *make coffee, make a cake, make a plan, make a decision* (you create it in your head), *make noise, make money*. Also two chunks to just remember: **make a mistake**, **make a phone call**.
- **do** ≈ **tasks, jobs and activities**, often things you have to do or do regularly: *do homework, do the dishes, do the shopping, do exercise, do a course, do business, do your best*. Also when we don't name the activity: *What are you doing? I have nothing to do.*

Indonesian doesn't help: *membuat* is sometimes do and *melakukan* is sometimes make. Trust the chunk, not the translation.

id.text:
Ini panduan kasar (berlaku untuk sebagian besar kasus, tapi tidak semuanya):
- **make** ≈ kamu **menciptakan atau menghasilkan** sesuatu yang tadinya tidak ada: *make coffee* (bikin kopi), *make a cake, make a plan* (membuat rencana), *make a decision* (mengambil keputusan: kamu 'menciptakannya' di kepala), *make noise* (berisik), *make money* (cari uang). Dua paket lagi yang tinggal dihafal: **make a mistake** (membuat kesalahan), **make a phone call** (menelepon).
- **do** ≈ **tugas, pekerjaan dan kegiatan**, sering hal yang wajib atau rutin: *do homework* (mengerjakan PR), *do the dishes* (mencuci piring), *do the shopping* (belanja), *do exercise* (berolahraga), *do a course* (ikut kursus), *do business* (berbisnis), *do your best* (berusaha sebaik mungkin). Juga saat kegiatannya tidak disebut: *What are you doing?* (Lagi ngapain?) *I have nothing to do.* (Aku nggak ada kerjaan.)

Bahasa Indonesia tidak membantu di sini: *membuat* kadang jadi do, *melakukan* kadang jadi make. Percayai paketnya, bukan terjemahannya.

rows.en: Can you make some coffee for the guests?
rows.id: Bisa bikinkan kopi untuk para tamu?

rows.en: My sister makes good money as a programmer.
rows.id: Kakak saya dapat penghasilan bagus sebagai programmer.

rows.en: I do the shopping on Saturday mornings.
rows.id: Saya belanja setiap Sabtu pagi.

rows.en: Don't worry about the result. Just do your best.
rows.id: Jangan khawatir soal hasilnya. Berusaha saja sebaik mungkin.
rows.note: do your best = berusaha sebaik mungkin

id.note: do your best = berusaha sebaik mungkin

rows.en: Pak Hasan does business with companies in Singapore.
rows.id: Pak Hasan berbisnis dengan perusahaan-perusahaan di Singapura.

blocks.text:
**Exceptions to remember** (they don't follow the guide):
- **make the bed** (merapikan tempat tidur) is a housework task, but it's *make*.
- **make breakfast / dinner** (you create food), but **do the cooking** (the job of cooking).
- **make a phone call** and **make a mistake** don't really 'create' anything: they're just chunks.

**Both are correct**: British English also says **take a decision**; people say **do a course** or **take a course**; and **do exercise** or **get exercise**.

id.text:
**Pengecualian yang perlu diingat** (tidak ikut panduan):
- **make the bed** (merapikan tempat tidur) itu pekerjaan rumah, tapi pakai *make*.
- **make breakfast / dinner** (kamu 'menciptakan' makanan), tapi **do the cooking** (tugas memasak).
- **make a phone call** dan **make a mistake** sebenarnya tidak 'menciptakan' apa-apa: hafalkan saja sebagai paket.

**Dua-duanya benar**: bahasa Inggris British juga bilang **take a decision**; orang bilang **do a course** atau **take a course**; dan **do exercise** atau **get exercise**.

blocks.prompt: Every morning before work, Dimas ___ his bed.
blocks.explain: make the bed is an exception: it's housework, but the chunk is make the bed. Dimas = he, so makes.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Every morning before work, Dimas ___ his bed.
id.explain: make the bed itu pengecualian: memang pekerjaan rumah, tapi paketnya make the bed (merapikan tempat tidur). Dimas = he, jadi makes.

blocks.text:
Indonesian *bilang, mengatakan, memberi tahu, berbicara, ngobrol* become four English verbs:
- **tell + a person** (the one who hears): *tell me, tell Rina, tell your boss*. Also four fixed chunks: **tell a story, tell a joke, tell the truth, tell a lie**.
- **say + the words**: *say hello, say sorry, say goodbye, say something, say yes*. To add the person, use **to**: *say sorry **to** your sister*. Never *say me*.
- **speak + a language**, and in more formal situations: *speak English, speak Javanese, Can I speak to the manager, please?*
- **talk** = a conversation between people: **talk to / with** someone, **talk about** something. Not *talk English*.

id.text:
*Bilang, mengatakan, memberi tahu, berbicara, ngobrol* dalam bahasa Inggris jadi empat kata kerja:
- **tell + orang** (yang mendengar): *tell me* (kasih tahu aku), *tell Rina, tell your boss*. Juga empat paket tetap: **tell a story** (bercerita), **tell a joke** (melucu), **tell the truth** (berkata jujur), **tell a lie** (berbohong).
- **say + kata-katanya**: *say hello* (menyapa), *say sorry* (minta maaf), *say goodbye* (pamit), *say something, say yes*. Untuk menyebut orangnya, pakai **to**: *say sorry **to** your sister*. Jangan pernah *say me*.
- **speak + bahasa**, dan di situasi yang lebih resmi: *speak English* (berbahasa Inggris), *speak Javanese, Can I speak to the manager, please?* (Bisa bicara dengan manajernya?)
- **talk** = percakapan antar orang, ngobrol: **talk to / with** seseorang, **talk about** sesuatu. Bukan *talk English*.

rows.en: Please tell your manager about the problem.
rows.id: Tolong beri tahu manajermu soal masalahnya.

rows.en: Budi never tells lies.
rows.id: Budi tidak pernah berbohong.

rows.en: He said goodbye to everyone and left.
rows.id: Dia pamit ke semua orang lalu pergi.

rows.en: Do you speak English at work?
rows.id: Kamu pakai bahasa Inggris di kantor?

rows.en: We talked about our plans for the holiday.
rows.id: Kami ngobrol soal rencana liburan kami.

blocks.text:
Quick test:
- A **person** right after the verb? → **tell** (*tell me*).
- The **words** themselves? → **say** (*say hello*).
- A **language**? → **speak** (*speak Japanese*).
- A **conversation**? → **talk** (*talk about work*).

Not a broken rule: **speak to** and **talk to** a person are both correct. *Speak to* sounds a bit more formal or serious (*I need to speak to you* can mean there's a problem); *talk to* is everyday.

id.text:
Tes cepat:
- Ada **orang** tepat setelah kata kerjanya? → **tell** (*tell me*).
- Yang disebut **kata-katanya**? → **say** (*say hello*).
- Sebuah **bahasa**? → **speak** (*speak Japanese*).
- Sebuah **obrolan**? → **talk** (*talk about work*).

Bukan pelanggaran aturan: **speak to** dan **talk to** seseorang dua-duanya benar. *Speak to* terdengar sedikit lebih resmi atau serius (*I need to speak to you* bisa berarti ada masalah); *talk to* untuk sehari-hari.

blocks.text: Indonesian traps: *bilang ke saya / kasih tahu saya* → **tell me** (not *say me*); *dia bisa bahasa Jepang* → *she **speaks** Japanese* (not *talks Japanese*); *minta maaf* → **say sorry**; *berkata jujur* → **tell the truth**; *ngobrol* → **talk** (or *chat*).

id.text: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *bilang ke saya / kasih tahu saya* → **tell me** (bukan *say me*); *dia bisa bahasa Jepang* → *she **speaks** Japanese* (bukan *talks Japanese*); *minta maaf* → **say sorry**; *berkata jujur* → **tell the truth**; *ngobrol* → **talk** (atau *chat*).

blocks.prompt: Dimas, can you ___ that again? I didn't hear you.
blocks.explain: that = the words Dimas just said, and no person comes after the verb, so use say: say that again. tell needs a person (tell me); talk is a conversation.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Dimas, can you ___ that again? I didn't hear you.
id.explain: that = kata-kata yang baru diucapkan Dimas, dan tidak ada orang setelah kata kerjanya, jadi pakai say: say that again (ulangi lagi). tell butuh orang (tell me); talk itu obrolan.

blocks.text:
Three very common verbs that often **don't** translate as *punya, ambil, dapat*:
- **have** + meals, events and experiences: *have breakfast / lunch / dinner, have a meeting, have a party, have a good time, have a rest*. Here *have* doesn't mean *punya*: *have lunch* = *makan siang*.
- **take** + photos, transport, medicine, breaks and seats: *take a photo, take a taxi, take the KRL, take an ojek, take medicine, take a break, take a seat*. (It's **an** ojek because *ojek* starts with a vowel sound, 'o'.)
- **get** = **receive** (*get a message*), **find** (*get a job*), **become** (*get better, get tired*) or **arrive** (*get home, get to the office*).

Why *get home* but *get **to** the office*? **home** works without *to* after verbs of movement: *go home, come home, get home*.

id.text:
Tiga kata kerja yang sangat umum dan sering **tidak** diterjemahkan jadi *punya, ambil, dapat*:
- **have** + makan, acara dan pengalaman: *have breakfast / lunch / dinner* (sarapan / makan siang / makan malam), *have a meeting* (rapat), *have a party* (mengadakan pesta), *have a good time* (bersenang-senang), *have a rest* (istirahat). Di sini *have* bukan *punya*: *have lunch* = *makan siang*.
- **take** + foto, kendaraan, obat, jeda dan tempat duduk: *take a photo* (memotret), *take a taxi, take the KRL, take an ojek* (naik taksi, KRL, ojek), *take medicine* (minum obat), *take a break* (rehat), *take a seat* (duduk). (Pakai **an** ojek karena *ojek* diawali bunyi vokal 'o'.)
- **get** = **menerima** (*get a message*: dapat pesan), **mendapat** (*get a job*: dapat kerja), **menjadi** (*get better*: membaik, *get tired*: jadi capek) atau **sampai** (*get home*: sampai rumah, *get to the office*: sampai kantor).

Kenapa *get home* tapi *get **to** the office*? **home** dipakai tanpa *to* setelah kata kerja gerak: *go home, come home, get home*.

rows.en: We usually have lunch at a warung near the office.
rows.id: Kami biasanya makan siang di warung dekat kantor.

rows.en: Did you have a good time in Yogyakarta?
rows.id: Kamu senang-senang di Yogyakarta?

rows.en: I take the KRL from Bogor every morning.
rows.id: Saya naik KRL dari Bogor setiap pagi.

rows.en: Let's take a short break and continue at three.
rows.id: Ayo rehat sebentar dan lanjut jam tiga.
rows.note: take a break (have a break is fine too)

id.note: take a break (have a break juga benar)

rows.en: I got a message from the bank this morning.
rows.id: Saya dapat pesan dari bank tadi pagi.

rows.en: It's getting late. Let's go home.
rows.id: Sudah makin malam. Ayo pulang.

blocks.text: **Both are fine**, so don't worry about these: **have a shower / take a shower** (mandi), **have a break / take a break**, **have a look / take a look** (lihat), **have a seat / take a seat** (silakan duduk), **get a taxi / take a taxi**, **have a rest / get some rest** (istirahat). British English uses *have* a bit more; American English uses *take* a bit more.

id.text: **Dua-duanya benar**, jadi tidak perlu khawatir: **have a shower / take a shower** (mandi), **have a break / take a break** (rehat), **have a look / take a look** (lihat), **have a seat / take a seat** (silakan duduk), **get a taxi / take a taxi** (naik/cari taksi), **have a rest / get some rest** (istirahat). Bahasa Inggris British sedikit lebih sering pakai *have*; American sedikit lebih sering pakai *take*.

blocks.text: Indonesian traps: *minum obat* → **take** medicine (not *drink medicine*); *ambil foto / foto-foto* → **take a photo** (not *make a photo*); *naik KRL / ojek* → **take** the KRL / an ojek; *sarapan* → **have breakfast**; *sampai rumah* → **get home** (*arrive home* is correct too, but *get home* is the everyday chunk; not *get to home*).

id.text: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *minum obat* → **take** medicine (bukan *drink medicine*); *ambil foto / foto-foto* → **take a photo** (bukan *make a photo*); *naik KRL / ojek* → **take** the KRL / an ojek; *sarapan* → **have breakfast**; *sampai rumah* → **get home** (*arrive home* juga benar, tapi *get home* yang paling umum sehari-hari; bukan *get to home*).

blocks.prompt: You look really tired. Why don't you ___ a rest?
blocks.explain: Rest (istirahat) is an experience, so it goes with have: have a rest. make and do never go with rest.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: You look really tired. Why don't you ___ a rest?
id.explain: Rest (istirahat) adalah pengalaman, jadi pasangannya have: have a rest. make dan do tidak pernah dipakai dengan rest.

id.intro: Hai! Dalam bahasa Inggris ada kata-kata yang memang berpasangan: kita make a mistake (membuat kesalahan), do our homework (mengerjakan PR), tell the truth (berkata jujur) dan take a photo (memotret). Di pelajaran ini kamu akan belajar pasangan paling berguna dari make dan do, say, tell, speak dan talk, serta have, take dan get, supaya kamu berhenti menerjemahkan kata per kata. Pemanasan: apa bahasa Inggrisnya 'minum obat'?
suggestedQuestions: Ada aturan untuk make dan do, atau harus dihafal saja?
Yang benar 'have a shower' atau 'take a shower'?

assessment.col-1: Lengkapi dengan make atau do: Pak Hasan has to ___ a decision about the new office before Friday.
assessment.col-2: Lengkapi dengan bentuk make atau do yang tepat: In our house, my brother always ___ the dishes after dinner.
assessment.col-3: Perbaiki kesalahannya: Can you say me the way to the station?
assessment.col-4: Bu Ani besar di Surabaya dan kuliah di Tokyo. Lengkapi dengan bentuk say, tell, speak atau talk yang tepat: She ___ Javanese, Indonesian and Japanese.
assessment.col-5: Perbaiki kesalahannya: Excuse me, could you make a photo of us in front of Monas?
assessment.col-6: Lengkapi dengan bentuk have, take atau get yang tepat: The traffic was terrible, so Budi didn't ___ home until 9 p.m.
assessment.col-7: Lengkapi dengan bentuk have, take atau get yang tepat: Sari is ___ a party at her kos on Saturday. Do you want to come?
